title: Olight Warrior Ultra + Free i3E flashlight $125.97 (RRP: A$209.95) Delivered @ Olight AU
body:
Deal: Olight Warrior Ultra + Free i3E flashlight $125.97 (RRP: A$209.95) Delivered @ Olight AU

[squattington] Love the imini 2! Managed to grab one from the last sale (with the free i3E) and it's one of my favourite gadgets. Use it nearly every day at work.
[michael9865] IMALENT MS03: 13,000 lumens would be better, usually on special for similar price
[ihbh] Who are the noobs that buy these torches? Those that like dressing up as GI Joe?
[Maxxiz] People actually doing GI Joe stuff I'd imagine
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] so if these people are cross dressing because of this light.
then what is the one you recommend?? I notice comments like this often doesn't mention the other better product. gatekeeping?
[rumblytangara] You've never had a use for a relatively high power, compact flashlight?
I've been using stuff like this for decades- LED developments have been a real gift.
[ihbh] My most powerful is this one: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/756098 - the kids love using it to go possum spotting in the backyard, etc.
But for camping, etc., I mostly use Ultrafire knock-offs that use 18650 batteries that can be swapped out easily. On Haul you can get two for < $5. Have been using these for many years.
[rumblytangara] So what's the issue with someone buying a decently made torch with a trustworthy IP rating for the price of a couple of Happy Meals? Maybe backyard hammock surfing or car camping is pretty low stakes, but there are so many easy ways to get into situations where reliable lighting is very, very important.
I've got cheapie lights too, but there is a time and a place for them. i.e. around the house. And I would never buy a torch branded by Energiser- I would not regard that as a serious lighting brand. Especially if it is purely rechargeable.
(If I didn't already just buy a jacket-mounted light, I'd be tempted to pick up the $70 one.)
[ihbh] @rumblytangara:
So what's the issue with someone buying
Nothing at all. See MS Paint's comment.
[rumblytangara] @ihbh:
Who are the noobs that buy these torches? Those that like dressing up as GI Joe?
Well, TIL that I'm apparently GI Joe despite being old enough to have owned Maglites with incandescent bulbs.
[ihbh] @rumblytangara:
And I would never buy a torch branded by Energiser- I would not regard that as a serious lighting brand
To each their own. Check out the price and the specs. It is a top notch torch for $14.25 (Powerpass).
[rumblytangara] @ihbh: Yes, to each their own. Which is why it's weird to bag people for wanting to buy flashlights from a recognised brand even if your own preference is for something else.
Personally, I don't bother looking at lumen specs anymore. Lumens are an easy hurdle with current LED tech. There are so many other things that are more relevant to good flashlights like beam spread, colour temp, swappable batteries, usability with gloves, I could go on.
Edit: A friend with the most powerful flashlight I have ever seen uses it to help navigate a 35 foot sailboat at night. So yeah, people use lights for different things besides possum spotting.
